biomes.name: Desert
biomes.blurb: Cheapest starter land. Dry and sandy. Good for small, hardy dinosaurs that lived in hot places.
biomes.grows: Dry scrub and tough succulents. Seeds take root slowly; the cheapest land is also the slowest garden.

biomes.name: Marsh
biomes.blurb: Wet, reedy lowland. Mid-priced. Suits swamp and shoreline species and the occasional rare draw.
biomes.grows: Reeds, ferns and water plants. The wettest land grows the most free grazing in the park.

biomes.name: Plains
biomes.blurb: Premium open grassland. The most versatile land in the park. Most big herbivores feel at home here.
biomes.grows: Open grassland. Steady regrowth and room to roam; the all-rounder.

_notes: M3 carry-over: colours pushed apart so the three biomes are unmistakable in the survey map, the living view and the legend: desert = sandy yellow, marsh = blue-teal, plains = bright grass green. `texture` picks the ground marks drawn on an owned parcel (sand dots / reed clumps and puddles / grass tufts). M4: parcels no longer carry a biome. Unowned land draws as neutral `unowned` scrub; the buyer picks a biome in the buy dialog and can Re-landscape later. `grows` is the biome guide line in the Real Estate office (growth rates are in balance.vegetation).

unowned.name: Scrub
unowned.blurb: Unsurveyed scrub. Buy it and choose Desert, Plains or Marsh.
